investigations.summary: PMM-T2663 (mysqlPerfschemaChangeAgent.spec.ts, added by #1777 the day before) failed in all 6 MySQL compat lanes on pmm-client 3.8.0/3.8.1 with 'unknown flag --skip-connection-check': the flag shipped in 3.9.0 (absent at percona/pmm v3.8.1), and the test had no version gate, the same defect #1781 fixed for PMM-T2534. Reproduced on a CHAOS VM with the 3.8.1 client and MySQL 8.4; the fix gates it at 3.9.0 (25 passed, T2663 skipped on the VM).

PSMDB Shard 7.x (latest client): PMM-T2445 timed out because mongodb_up never reached 1 after the change agent call with --skip-connection-check. 3.8.1 · Percona Server 8.4: PMM-T2528's slowlog agent disable returned OK, but PMM Server kept the agent Running instead of 'Done (disabled)'. Both are the open PMM-15835 lost update (a ChangeAgent racing the agent's status report) that nights 107 and 109 already traced. Matched to the ticket from the job logs; not re-reproduced.

ui @gcp: for the third night running only the GCP PostgreSQL 13 fixture (gc-postgres13) failed: Add service got 'Connection check failed: dial tcp 34.71.152.234:5432: i/o timeout', and the 3 tests that depend on it failed after it; the other GCP instances passed. Same failure as night 109 and its re-run #12301; 34.71.152.234:5432 does not answer from the runner host either. No pmm-qa change can fix it: someone with GCP access must restore the Cloud SQL instance or its authorized networks, or drop pgsql13 from verifyGCRemoteInstance_test.js if it was retired.

ha backup-restore #50: PMM-T2289 (new in #1624) found No data in the HA Health Overview 'PostgreSQL Pods' Role/Replication cells for pmm-ha-pg-db-instance1-vzcm-0, because that pod's PMM sidecar registered its PostgreSQL service at install but never its -patroni-external service. The gap was already there before the backup and restore, so the restore did not cause it, and the test is right to fail. This is the open, intermittent sidecar-registration race PMM-15794 (the operator's prerun script runs the add commands once with no retry, and sidecar mode does not re-run it); the evidence was added to the ticket. Diagnosed from the build's trace and inventory artifacts: 3 CHAOS HA clusters were tried and failed on infrastructure, so it was not reproduced.

compat client 3.7.1: PMM Server (3-dev-latest) missed pmm3-aws-staging-start's 100 s readyz budget on a slow EC2 instance (image pull 129 s against 35-45 s on its siblings). After Grafana's slow first start, pmm-managed restarted Grafana 'to apply alert rule changes' it had already loaded 26 s earlier (the PMM-14956 startup restart in managed/services/alerting/provisioning.go), which pushed readiness past the budget. Without that restart readyz would have been 200 about 7 s before the deadline. Reproduced the redundant restart on a CHAOS VM (8-17 s each time); the faithful re-run #1450 passed. The budget should not be raised.

nightly ha: the EKS PMM HA server was healthy at 20:03-20:06 (pods Ready, /ping and settings PUT 200), but the GitHub jobs sat queued about 18 min, and from 20:24 to 20:28 every shard's readiness check got /v1/server/readyz 500, so no tests ran. No server-side logs survived: the readiness step skips the log download, and cleanup deleted the cluster, so the cause can't be shown (spot nodegroup, PG pods rolled at 20:02, a pg backup pod in Error are unproven candidates). The faithful re-run #1451 stayed readyz 200 for 30+ min past install and its GitHub run passed 5/5 jobs with tests executed. Suggest saving the readyz body and logs.zip when that step fails.
